facts.text: Ealing Studios, founded in 1902, launched the world’s first feature film and today remains a major force in film and television production.
The Great Western Railway opened Ealing Broadway station in 1838, turning the area from a rural village into a commuter hub.
Ealing earned the nickname “Queen of the Suburbs” during the 20th century, reflecting its rapid suburban growth and community spirit.
Local archivist Dr Jonathan Oates preserves Ealing’s stories, ensuring that tales from the 100‑year‑old Gunnersbury Park and other landmarks stay alive.
Ealing’s history stretches back to Saxon times, evolving from a quiet settlement into a bustling London borough by the mid‑20th century.
